root_cause.text: In the IPv4 FIB flush path, fib_table_flush() wrongly skipped error routes (such as blackhole routes) unless flush_all was set, even when their attached nexthop object had been marked dead, so those routes retained references to the deleted nexthop and its device.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “error routes are not flushed when their nexthop object is deleted” and therefore “keep holding a reference on the nexthop object”; the patch changes net/ipv4/fib_trie.c so the skip condition for error routes now applies only when `!(fi->fib_flags & RTNH_F_DEAD)`, meaning dead-nexthop error routes must be flushed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allow non-full fib table flushes to delete error routes that are already marked dead while still preserving active error routes.
intent_record.what: The condition that skips flushing certain routes in fib_table_flush() was tightened by adding an extra check for !(fi->fib_flags & RTNH_F_DEAD), and the accompanying comment was updated to say that when not flushing the entire table, error routes are skipped only if they are not marked for deletion.
intent_record.how: At runtime, partial flushes no longer preserve all error routes unconditionally; error routes flagged with RTNH_F_DEAD are now allowed to be flushed, while non-dead error routes are still skipped. This fixes behavior so routes already marked for deletion are actually removed during a non-full table flush.

candidates.rationale: This condition unconditionally skips error routes during non-full flushes based only on route type, failing to account for routes whose nexthop has already been marked dead. That logic is the direct cause of retaining references to deleted nexthops/devices.
This continue enforces the buggy skip path for error routes in non-full flushes, preventing removal of dead error routes and leaving stale nexthop/device references intact.

As a result, dead blackhole/error routes retain references to deleted nexthops and devices.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant logic in `fib_table_flush()` clearly enough to decide. The vulnerable behavior was that error routes were skipped unless `flush_all` was set, even when their nexthop handling did not mark them dead. In this commit, the function signature was changed to `int fib_table_flush(struct net *net, struct fib_table *tb, bool flush_all)`, and the filtering logic was updated. Specifically, the old condition `if (!fi || !(fi->fib_flags & RTNH_F_DEAD) || tb->tb_id != fa->tb_id)` was replaced with `if (!fi || tb->tb_id != fa->tb_id || (!(fi->fib_flags & RTNH_F_DEAD) && !fib_props[fa->fa_type].error))`, which means error routes are no longer skipped solely because `RTNH_F_DEAD` is not set. In addition, the new explicit check `if (!flush_all && fib_props[fa->fa_type].error) { ... continue; }` preserves non-namespace-dismantle behavior while allowing error routes to be flushed when `flush_all` is true. This matches the commit message root-cause description and implements the fix.
